hypotheses.mechanism: The detector reads every frame with a strided slice zarr[t, ::1, ::4, ::4] at phase (0,0). Training does the same (tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py _load_frame l.217, train_unet_transformer.py l.340, no phase jitter), and 100% of raw ILP nodes in friend A's cache have y,x = 0 mod 4 (checked on 5 raw geffs). So (i) every node sits on an isotropic 1.625 um grid: quantisation RMS 0.47 um per axis, 0.81 um in 3D; (ii) the detector has only ever seen 1/16 of the xy pixels of each train video. Measured on the exp39 final graph (30 videos, rounded coordinates): median distance from a GT node to the nearest prediction is 1.68 um (44b6) and 1.82 um (6bba); 17% / 27% are > 2.5 um and 7.4% / 12.9% are > 3.5 um. The FN anatomy shows positional accuracy is the lever, not link choice. Swaps (1528 FN, du/dv median 4.35/4.48 um, oracle +0.032) and u_diverted/v_taken (1149 FN, median 3.9/4.4 um, oracle +0.016) are GT nodes that sit about 4 um from their matched prediction, between nuclei spaced 8.5-9.2 um apart, so the per-frame Hungarian matching flips. Local relinking moves do not fix them: on SELECTION, 245 swaps gave dTP -3 / dFP +6 and 15.8k repoints gave dTP -224 / dFP +409. Consistent with this, linefit is the largest post-processing stage (+0.0145) and x138's head (-10% centre error) gave +0.007 on the LB. Shift-and-stitch (OverFeat / FCN) supplies the 15/16 pixels the network has never seen and yields a 2-4x finer xy heatmap. Each existing peak can then be refined without changing the node set.
hypotheses.change: Inside predict_video, after the normal phase-(0,0) TTA peaks are extracted (node set, threshold and NMS unchanged), run the PRIMARY only (no rot/flip TTA) on 3 extra phase-shifted strided inputs zarr[t, :, dy::4, dx::4], (dy,dx) in {(0,2),(2,0),(2,2)}, or on all 15 if time allows. Interleave the logits into a fine xy grid (fine[4j+dy, 4i+dx] = logit_phase[j, i]). For each peak, take the fine-grid argmax within +-1 coarse cell, then a 3-point parabolic / DARK log-heatmap Taylor offset in y, x and also z (z is already stride 1). Clip the total shift to <= 1.2 um. Carry the float coords through association with the port's trilinear gather. Arms: (a) V1284 head alone (control); (b) polyphase alone; (c) average of the two estimates; (d) polyphase first, then the head residual. Cost is +3 forward passes per frame against the current 16 (2 models x 8 views), about +19% GPU time.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Classes it can touch: swap + u_diverted + v_taken oracle = +0.032 + 0.016 = +0.048 local; a_linefit 353 FN x 7.1e-6 per error unit (0.0323 / (1528 FN + 3003 FP)) = +0.0025. Quantisation share of error: before linefit (what relink, gap closing and safe-division see), grid noise is 3 x 0.22 = 0.66 um^2 of roughly 2-3 um^2 total MSE, i.e. 22-33%. After linefit (w 0.8, 5-point linear fit: i.i.d.-noise variance factor ~0.23), it is about 0.15 of 1.49 um^2 = 10% of MSE. Removing 3/4 of the xy and 1/2 of the z quantisation therefore cuts 5-15% RMS, the same order as the V1284 head's -10%, which bought +0.007 public. Because both largely remove the same grid error, the independent part on top of the port is <= +0.003. Extra recall from nuclei that fall between samples is not counted.
hypotheses.lab_test: Step 1, GPU capture: one Kaggle T4 kernel, primary only, 3 phases, 199 videos x 100 frames, ~1-2 GPU h. Share the kernel with the V1284 capture. For every raw node in friend A's cache (keyed by t,z,y,x grid), store the refined float zyx. Step 1 readout (no scorer): median distance to the matched GT node (official 7 um matching) must fall >= 8% on BOTH embryos against grid coords, and >= 3% against the head's coords. Step 2: Kaggle-CPU replay lab with refined coords substituted into the raw nodes, ILP topology and probs fixed. SELECTION, then one CONFIRMATION. Gate: >= +0.002 overall, >= +0.001 per embryo, >= 55% of videos gaining, 90% CI > 0, N_pred identical. This lab is less in-sample than any earlier TTA test: the phase-shifted pixels were never in the training data, which is why rot/flip TTA gains were 43-97% memorised and this should not be.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.004 public on top of the V1284 port (0 if fully redundant with the head); +0.003..+0.006 if shipped without the head. The proportional read of x138: -10% error = +0.007, and 5-15% RMS gives +0.003..+0.010 before overlap.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. Eric (rank 77) reported a sub-voxel peak refinement at +0.0078 local but -0.002 on the LB twice; the method is undisclosed and most likely interpolated the coarse heatmap, adding no new pixels. The learned x138 head did transfer (+0.007). The downstream gates (tight 5.5 um, gap 5.0 um, linefit 0.8) were tuned on grid coordinates and may need one re-check on float coords. CNNs are not exactly shift-equivariant, so check phase-to-phase consistency of the peak value (reject a peak's refinement if the phases disagree by > 1 coarse cell). The node count is unchanged by construction, so there is no multiplier artefact.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed TTA variants (rot90/transpose/axis flips/Z-flip) averaged views of the SAME pixels and were judged on detection; this adds the 15/16 never-seen pixels and changes only localisation, with the node set fixed. It is not the V1284 port: no learned head, a complementary input-side estimate that can be ensembled with it. It is not a detector fine-tune.

hypotheses.mechanism: linefit (weight 0.8, +-2 frames, linear, isotropic; exp39 cell 7 linefit_smooth_output_graph) is the largest post-processing stage (+0.0145 on 12 videos), but it has three defects. (i) It treats z and xy alike, although the measured residual std of predictions within 2.5 um of GT is z 1.03 um vs y 0.64 / x 0.66 um (30 videos): z is ~2.5x noisier in variance, and 6bba carries a z bias of -0.61 um. (ii) It skips every node whose chain hits a fork or an end within +-1 (len(neighbourhood) < 3). Division parents and daughters therefore get no smoothing, yet divisions need ~3 um accuracy (Lime1123; kevin park found 39% of division nodes > 3 um off), and the public division J is only 0.36. (iii) It runs only at the very end, so the motion relink, gap closing, safe divisions and DaughterNet geometry all use raw 1.625-um-grid positions and velocities from integer differences. Meanwhile a_linefit = 353 FN are GT links lost BECAUSE the uniform 0.8 weight moved a node out of its match on turning or accelerating cells. SOTA trackers (u-track, TrackMate LAP/Kalman, KIT-Sch-GE interpolation) use per-axis measurement noise with a motion model.
hypotheses.change: Replace linefit with a per-segment Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother: constant-velocity model, per-axis measurement noise r_z, r_xy and process noise q, estimated per VIDEO from innovation statistics (label-free, so it adapts to each unseen embryo). Add 3-sigma outlier gating or a Huber update so one bad detection is not dragged. Split tracks at forks: the parent segment ends at the parent node and each daughter segment starts at its daughter, giving one-sided smoothing instead of none. Variant B also runs the smoother once BEFORE the motion relink, so the Hungarian and gap closing see smoothed positions and velocities. Lab grid (<= 12 configs): r_z/r_xy in {1, 2, 3} x q scale {0.5, 1, 2} x fork one-sided on/off, plus pre-relink on/off. The control is the B28 isotropic optimum (w 0.8, window 2).
hypotheses.upper_bound: End-only variant (topology and N_pred identical): a_linefit 353 FN x 7.1e-6 = +0.0025. Part of the far-GT population (swap/u_div/v_taken, oracle +0.048), whose matched offsets of 3.5-4.5 um sit near the decision boundary between nuclei 8.5-9.2 um apart. Divisions: local TP 23 / FP 43 / FN 128. On the public board every +0.04 of division J is +0.004 score, so 0.36 -> 0.40 gives +0.004. Realistic ceiling about +0.005.
hypotheses.lab_test: Kaggle-CPU replay lab on friend A's cache: add rts_smooth to the tail in place of linefit. SELECTION grid, then one CONFIRMATION. Gate: >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, >= 55% of videos, CI > 0. Report dJ separately from the multiplier (the multiplier must be exactly 1.000 for the end-only variant) and division TP/FP. Secondary readout: median distance to matched GT for division nodes and for all nodes, both embryos. Re-run the winner once on float coords from the V1284 / polyphase capture, since the noise ratios change.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.003 local and public. Post-processing settings chosen locally transfer (hikaggler, Justin CH123), and the end-only variant cannot hit the node-multiplier trap.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low to medium. It uses no network outputs, so it is not an in-sample trust issue, and the per-video noise estimate is label-free. Risks: 44b6 labels are very sparse (0.2-1.3% coverage), so that embryo may show no signal and fail the per-embryo gate. The pre-relink variant changes topology and inherits the relink's poor transfer (+0.001-class on LB), so ship the end-only variant unless pre-relink wins clearly on both embryos.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B28 closed only the isotropic weight x window grid of the existing linear fit. The closed relink knobs are gates and bonuses; this changes the position and velocity estimates. Per-axis noise, one-sided smoothing at forks, per-video noise estimation and outlier gating are new mechanisms. Global-shift relink and constant offset correction are different: those are shifts, not smoothing.

hypotheses.mechanism: linajea (Malin-Mayor et al., light-sheet zebrafish/mouse/Drosophila lineages learned from SPARSE annotations, the same regime as ours) predicts for every cell a parent vector, the offset to its position at t-1. Candidate link costs use |child + pv(child) - parent|, and divisions appear where two children point at one parent. Our pipeline has no such signal. The relink extrapolates own velocity from integer grid differences, which picks the true child in 0 of 381 contested cases (Le Quang Canh). DaughterNet v1 insertion runs at 27% precision against a public break-even of 26.5%; about 45% is needed for a visible gain, and the daughter side (AUC 0.74-0.77) is the weak link. The swap-anatomy agent measured that geometry-only criteria (acceleration, length) do not separate good from bad local moves. x138 shows that a tiny MLP on the frozen 224-d UNet features (7 x 32 channels at and around the peak) transfers to the LB, and the TemporalUNet features are computed over a temporal window, so they carry motion information.
hypotheses.change: Use the same Kaggle capture as the V1284 port (224-d features per peak on all 199 videos; add the t-1 frame's features if cheap). Train on CPU in minutes a ridge regressor or MLP 224 -> 64 -> 3 that regresses, for each prediction matched to a GT node with a GT parent, the offset to the GT parent's position (122k TP edges; daughters learn their parent offset), with 5 folds by leak group. Uses: (a) in tools/div_insert.py add e_div = |D1 + pv(D1) - P| + |D2 + pv(D2) - P| and |pv(D1) + pv(D2)| (sister symmetry) as ranking features next to DaughterNet p, same caps and steal logic; (b) optionally, in the relink, for targets with >= 2 sources inside the gate, replace the own-velocity motion distance by |target + pv(target) - source|. Arm (a) ships first.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Division term: public division J 0.36, worth 0.1 x J. Lifting added-fork precision from 27% to 45% at the same cap would take J to about 0.40-0.45: +0.004..+0.009. Edge term: break 399 FN (oracle +0.003) plus contested diversions where the true parent is detected (a subset of the +0.016 oracle). Realistic total ceiling about +0.01.
hypotheses.lab_test: OOF readout first: median |x_t + pv - x_{t-1}^GT| must be >= 25% below the velocity baseline |x_t - (x_t - x_{t-1}^pred) - x_{t-1}^GT| on both embryos. In contested cases (>= 2 predicted predecessors within 7 um) the head must pick the GT parent >= 70% of the time. Then the replay lab: DaughterNet insertion + e_div on SELECTION, target added-fork precision >= 0.45 (v1: 4/15). One CONFIRMATION with the existing gate (>= +0.002, CI > 0, net TP >= +3, precision >= 0.31).
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.004 public, mostly from the division term; edge gains are likely <= +0.001 on the LB, per the forum's linker experience.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium-high. The frozen features come from a detector trained on all 199 videos, so even fold-trained heads see in-sample features; the x138 head had the same issue and transferred. The public test holds few divisions (J 0.36 on perhaps 10-30 events), so +-1 event is +-0.003 noise. The relink arm inherits the relink's weak transfer.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Closed division lines (DivNet veto, B32 pair model closed at candidate reach, the DaughterNet v1/v2 grids) all score appearance at candidate nodes; none uses a learned per-cell displacement. B8 (parent-offset head, linajea/ELEPHANT) was queued at P2 and never run. The closed flow-prior relink uses the median displacement of neighbours, not a learned per-cell vector.

hypotheses.mechanism: Ultrack, the organisers' own tracker, generates an over-complete set of detection hypotheses and lets the tracking ILP choose which nodes exist together with the links. Our node set is fixed by a hard 0.965 threshold before linking, and the ILP is tracksdata ILPSolver(edge_weight * edge_prob, appearance, disappearance, division) with node_weight left at 0 (verified: the parameter exists and accepts an Attr expression). Measured: 7.4% / 12.9% of GT nodes (44b6 / 6bba) have no prediction within 3.5 um; a_never = 1907 FN (31% of FN); B35 step A showed a 0.90-threshold pass reaches 151/151 GT divisions (vs 136) at +24% candidate nodes. The missing nuclei are in the heatmap; the failure is selection. Readmit and gapfill (x138/thtennant, neutral on the LB) pick sub-threshold peaks by local rules (only near open ends, only on straight interpolations). Here the transformer scores edges to the optional peaks and the global ILP accepts one only when its links pay for its explicit cost.
hypotheses.change: In predict_video, extract peaks at threshold 0.6 with the same 3 um NMS (confident peaks suppress optional ones). Tag p < 0.965 as optional and let the edge transformer score the enlarged kNN graph as now. Call ILPSolver(..., node_weight = lambda * max(0, logit(0.965) - logit(p))), everything else unchanged. Nodes outside the solution are dropped, as today. In post-processing, stop the motion relink from attaching optional nodes to anything the ILP did not link them to: keep their ILP edges, so the relink cannot turn them into free extra nodes. Sweep lambda so N_pred rises <= +1%.
hypotheses.upper_bound: a_never 1907 FN x 7.1e-6 = +0.0135 local if all were recovered at zero cost; part of the far-GT swap/diversion population (oracle +0.048) is also reachable. Node cost: each +1% N_pred = -0.001 x J (about -0.0009). A realistic capture of 10-20% of a_never is +0.0015..+0.003, minus <= 0.0009 node cost.
hypotheses.lab_test: Needs a GPU rebuild of the raw ILP graphs for 199 videos at threshold 0.6 with node probs and the lambda-weighted ILP: 3-5 Kaggle T4 hours split over 2-4 kernels. Alternatively dump the 0.6 candidate graph once and solve the ILP for each lambda on Kaggle CPU. Replay lab: SELECTION grid lambda in {0.5, 1, 2, 4}, then one CONFIRMATION. Gates: the standard +0.002 / per-embryo +0.001 / 55% / CI, plus N_pred <= control +1%, and the gain must come from dJ, not the multiplier, on each embryo. Readout: the share of 6bba GT nodes with no prediction within 3.5 um must drop from 12.9% to <= 11%.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: High. Node-set changes have repeatedly looked good offline and lost on the LB (min-track-length -0.004, det 0.99 -0.005). The edge transformer and the ILP weights were tuned on the 0.965 node distribution, and optional nodes are exactly where the network is least calibrated. The 2-day window is tight because this touches the GPU part of the pipeline. Rank it last; run it only if the capture kernel for the other hypotheses has spare GPU budget.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Readmit and gapfill are local heuristics outside the solver, and detector-threshold probes (A3, A29) changed the whole node set blindly. This keeps the confident set and makes each extra node pay through the global ILP objective with an explicit node cost, which is the Ultrack mechanism and has never been tried here. The B25 pruning and B31 clustering lines went the opposite way (removing nodes).
